illustration.alt: The companion on the woodland path, next to a little grey pebble and a flower.

companionLines.bo: Hi {nome}! There's a little voice in the wood. Shall we listen quietly?
companionLines.pilu: Hi {nome}! Can you hear? Someone in the wood is talking very softly.
companionLines.tango: Hi {nome}! Let's run into the wood! ...Wait. First we listen.

illustration.alt: Emma, with two messy bunches, a yellow coat and red wellies, walks into the wood with her basket; Grandma sits on a log at the edge.

screens.text: Emma has two bunches, red wellies and a little yellow coat. She goes into the wood. Grandma says: "I'll be right here."

illustration.alt: At the stream Emma holds a grey, round, smooth pebble that seems to smile; the water makes little splashes.

screens.text: At the stream Emma throws pebbles: plink, plonk, plink. Then she finds a round, smooth one. "Hey! Don't throw me!" says a little voice.

companionLines.bo: A little voice! I'm a bit scared. Can you hear it?
companionLines.pilu: Did you hear? Emma stops and listens.
companionLines.tango: Who said that? Let's look, quick! ...Wait. Let's listen.

illustration.alt: Emma sitting on the grass by the stream, with Pietrolino in the palm of her hand; two little birds on the branches.

screens.text: "I'm Pietrolino," says the pebble. "I talk to anyone who stops to listen." Emma sits down on the grass.

illustration.alt: Three pictures in a row: a water drop for the stream, a little bird, some dry leaves. Emma, beside them, listens with her eyes closed.

screens.text: Emma closes her eyes. The wood has lots of voices.

companionLines.bo: Let's listen too. One voice at a time.
companionLines.pilu: Can you hear how the wood talks? One voice at a time.
companionLines.tango: So many voices! ...Wait. One at a time.

lesson.together: Point to one picture at a time and just say: "This is the stream: plink, plonk". Then ask: "Where is the little bird?". At the end, point to one and ask: "What is it called?". If they touch a different picture, tell them that one's name, nothing more.

items.name: the stream
items.this: This is the stream: plink, plonk.

items.name: the little bird
items.this: This is the little bird: tweet, tweet.

items.name: the leaves
items.this: These are the leaves: swish, swish.

lesson.ask: And this one, what is it called?
lesson.done: The stream, the little bird, the leaves. The wood talks softly.

illustration.alt: Emma walks back to Grandma along the path, with her basket; Pietrolino peeks out of her coat pocket.

screens.text: Emma puts Pietrolino in her pocket and goes back to Grandma. From the pocket, a little voice: "Even a tiny pebble makes big circles."

companionLines.bo: Tomorrow I'll listen to the wood with you, {nome}. See you tomorrow.
companionLines.pilu: Tomorrow I'll close my eyes and listen, {nome}. See you tomorrow.
companionLines.tango: Tomorrow I'll stop for a minute and listen, {nome}. See you tomorrow!
